title: Keep the crown
intro: In the champion pattern the first value starts with the crown, and every later value challenges it: only a bigger one takes the crown. Today's values are Irish mountains, in metres.

rounds.name: heights
rounds.right: `highest` ends as {best}: {who} saw off every challenge after it took the crown.

why.yes: `{value} > {champ}` is false: {who} isn't higher, so the crown stays with {champName}. Only a bigger value takes it.
why.no: `{value} > {champ}` is true: {who} is higher than {champName}, so it takes the crown.

rounds.name: heights
rounds.right: Six values, one champion: {who}, {best} {unit}. Each challenger only had to beat the champion so far, never the whole array.

why.yes: `{value} > {champ}` is false: {who} isn't higher, so the crown stays with {champName}.
why.no: `{value} > {champ}` is true: {who} beats {champName}, so it takes the crown.

rounds.prompt: The twist: winter on the summit, every temperature below zero, and this version starts `highest` at 0. What does it print?
rounds.right: It prints 0, a temperature that isn't even in the array. Start the champion at `{name}[0]` and it would print {max}, the real highest.
rounds.why: `highest` starts at `0`, and no temperature here beats 0, so the crown never moves. What is `highest` still holding at the end?
